blocks.text: The Violation Ticket Lifecycle page in the Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) app enables you to fully configure the ticket lifecycle to accommodate your organization's specific operational needs, providing full transparency and control over how violation tickets are managed. By customizing your ticket lifecycle, you can create a streamlined, efficient, and tailored workflow. You can define violation ticket status transitions, set up workflows to automatically open new violation tickets or aggregate them within existing violation tickets, define conditions to trigger automatic dispatch to third-party vendors, and set rules to automatically lock a violation ticket.
The Violation Ticket Lifecycle page includes:

blocks.item: Violation Ticket Statuses: Set the status of a violation ticket within the violation ticket workflow. You can also create custom ticket statuses that allow you to tailor your ticketing system to specific business requirements. To learn more, see Managing Violation Ticket Statuses in AEM.
Violation Ticket Workflows: Configure automated rules for managing violation tickets. Violation ticket workflow categories include the following rule sets:
Violation Ticket Status Management: Define the rules to update the status of a violation ticket.
Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers: Define the rules to lock a violation ticket.
Auto-Dispatch to External Systems: Automate the creation of third-party work management items and alerts.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About Violation Tickets and Viewing Violation Tickets in AEM.

blocks.heading: Configuring Violation Ticket Workflow Rule Sets

blocks.text: To configure violation ticket workflow rule sets:

blocks.item: Go to the AEM app (Assets).
In the left-side navigation, click Settings > Violation Ticket Lifecycle.
The Violation Ticket Lifecycle page appears.
Click Violation Ticket Workflows.
See image.
The Violation Ticket Workflows page appears.
See image.
On the Violation Ticket Workflows page, configure rules for the following workflow categories:
Violation Ticket Status Management
To configure automated rules for violation tickets:
Click Violation Ticket Status Management.
The Violation Ticket Status Management drawer appears.
Click Unlink & Override to enable rule creation.
See image.
Click Create a New Rule.
The Violation Ticket Status Management drawer appears.
In the Violation Ticket Status Management drawer, enter the following details:
NAME: Enter a name for the rule.
CATEGORY: Select one of the following options:
Automatic Violation Ticket Closure
Set the conditions to close a violation ticket.
Set the criteria:
IF:
Violation Ticket status is: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
A third-party work management item is attached: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
(Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
THEN: From the Update violation ticket status to drop-down menu, select the action that should be taken for violation tickets that meet the IF condition.
See image.
Resurface Policy Violation - Create New Violation Ticket
Create a new violation ticket if a previously detected policy violation resurfaces.
Set the criteria:
IF:
Violation Ticket status is: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
At least one policy violation is active for: Enter the number of days. The rule is triggered even if one policy violation is active for the specified period.
A third-party work management item is attached: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
(Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
THEN: A new violation ticket is created with the resurfaced policy violation. This option is displayed by default.
See image.
Resurface Policy Violation - Reopen Violation Ticket
Reopen the violation ticket if a previously detected policy violation resurfaces.
Set the criteria:
IF:
Violation Ticket status is: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
At least one policy violation is active for: Enter the number of days. The rule is triggered even if one policy violation is active for the specified period.
A third-party work management item is attached: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
(Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
THEN: From the Move violation ticket to status drop-down menu, select the action that should be taken for violation tickets that meet the IF condition.
See image.
Custom Status Transition
Define custom conditions for the violation ticket status transition.
Set the criteria:
IF:
Violation Ticket status is: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
A third-party work management item is attached: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
(Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
THEN: From the Move violation ticket to status drop-down menu, select the action that should be taken for violation tickets that meet the IF condition.
See image.
See image.
(Optional) Click New Rule to add a new rule.
Save the rule set in one of the following ways:
Click Save for rules take effect when new data is ingested into your account.
Click Save & Run to save the rule set and immediately apply the rules on the tickets.
See image.
Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers
To configure automated rules to lock a violation ticket:
Click Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers.
The Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers drawer appears.
Click Unlink & Override to enable rule creation.
See image.
Click Create a New Rule.
The Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers drawer appears.
In the Lock Violation Ticket Scope Triggers drawer, enter the following details:
NAME: Enter a name for the rule.
Set the criteria:
IF:
Violation Ticket is manually split or merged: This checkbox is selected by default.
Violation Ticket status is: Select the violation ticket status for which this rule should be applied.
A third-party work management item is attached: Select the checkbox to apply the rule only to violation tickets linked to a third-party tool (e.g., Jira).
(Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
THEN: The violation ticket is locked. This option is displayed by default.
See image.
(Optional) Click New Rule to add a new rule.
Save the rule set in one of the following ways:
Click Save for rules to take effect when new data is ingested into your account.
Click Save & Run to save the rule set and immediately apply the rules on the tickets.
See image.
Auto-Dispatch to External Systems
To configure automated rules for creating third-party work management items and alerts:
Click Auto-Dispatch to External Systems.
The Auto-Dispatch to External Systems drawer appears.
See image.
Click Create a New Rule.
The Auto-Dispatch to External Systems drawer appears.
In the Auto-Dispatch to External Systems drawer, enter the following details:
NAME: Enter a name for the rule.
Set the criteria:
IF:
Violation Ticket status is: Select the checkbox to add the violation ticket status to which the rule should be applied.
Violation Ticket severity is: Select the checkbox to add the violation ticket severity to which the rule should be applied.
Violation Ticket assignee is: Select the checkbox to add the assignee of the violation ticket on which the rule should be applied.
(Optional) You can use the AND/OR operators to include additional criteria and create custom rules.
THEN:
Create a third-party item on: Select a value from the drop-down menu.
Create New Outegration: Click to configure an outegration for the third-party value selected previously.
See image.
(Optional) Click New Rule to add a new rule.
Save the rule set in one of the following ways:
Click Save for rules to take effect when new data is ingested into your account.
Click Save & Run to save the rule set and immediately apply the rules on the tickets.
See image.
Click Done.

blocks.text: You can view the activity log for all these actions on a ticket's Activity tab.
